extracted.intended_audience: short-story writers, editors, literary readers, and researchers seeking information about the O. Henry Award (eligibility, history, and selection)
extracted.subtask_description: Information and standards for what stories are eligible for the O. Henry Prize Stories anthology and how selections are made (history of prize formats, number of stories chosen, and geographic/translation eligibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarded for short stories of exceptional merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The O. Henry Award is an annual American award given to short stories of exceptional merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the stated standard of quality the prize recognizes — 'exceptional merit' in short fiction. The Wikipedia article situates the O. Henry Prize Stories alongside The Best American Short Stories as one of the two best-known annual anthologies of short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — publication in American or Canadian periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: All stories published in an American or Canadian periodical are eligible for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly limits eligibility to stories appearing in U.S. or Canadian periodicals (magazines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — translations allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible stories include stories that have been translated into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article states that translated stories published in eligible periodicals are considered, i.e., original-language publication outside English is acceptable if an English translation appears in an eligible periodical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection format — guest editor chooses twenty stories
rubrics_metrics.description: As of 2021 the guest editor chooses twenty short stories, each an O. Henry Prize story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The anthology is a curated collection of twenty stories selected by the guest editor; the 'twenty best stories' framing indicates a fixed-size annual anthology as the selection output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process — historical juror/prize formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Until 2002 there were first, second, and third prize winners and from 2003 to 2019 there were three jurors who each selected a short story of special interest or merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This documents that the method of recognizing and selecting stories has changed over time (ranked prizes early on, then juror-favorites, and later a guest-editor twenty-story selection). It implies different evaluative/selection practices across eras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic expansion of eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2022, the series opened to African magazines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates a broadened geographic scope of eligible periodicals beyond U.S. and Canadian outlets beginning in 2022, reflecting an evolving eligibility policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stated mission — strengthen the art of the short story
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of The O. Henry Prize Stories remains to strengthen the art of the short story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mission statement serves as a guiding principle for selection: selections should align with the anthology's aim to support and advance short-story art.
